subject: social-studies
title: The Globalisation Supply Chain of One Smartphone

slides.heading: The Globalisation Supply Chain of One Smartphone
bullets: How one smartphone crosses the world before it is sold: raw materials are mined in Country A, components are made in Country B, the phone is assembled in Country C, and only then is it shipped to a shop shelf in Singapore - value added at every handover
slides.notes: Welcome everyone in and say: today we follow one smartphone across four countries, where each stage hands the product on and adds value.

slides.heading: What we will learn
bullets: Explain how a global product crosses borders at every stage, stage by stage from mine to Singapore shelf
Show the chain in order: Country A mines raw materials ($10), Country B makes components ($35), Country C assembles ($70), Singapore sells ($120)
slides.notes: Read the two goals aloud and tell the class: by the end you will be able to run the whole supply chain in order and say what each stage adds.

slides.heading: One phone, one shop - so it was made here, right?
bullets: The phone is bought in one shop in Singapore and carries one brand on the box
Yet no single country made all of it - what journey did it take before it reached the shelf?
slides.notes: Ask the class: if the phone was sold here, was it made here? Take two or three answers, then say: hold them, because the animation shows a value bar rising in four different places, not one factory.

slides.heading: Value is added at every handover
bullets: Each stage does work the stage before could not: mining gives raw materials, component-making gives working parts, assembly gives a finished phone, and retail gives the buyer the product
The value-added bar rises at every handover - $10, then $35, then $70, then $120 - because every stage adds value along the chain
slides.notes: Stress the deciding idea: the stages were linked by a chain - the product was carried on by route arrows, and its value rose at each handover.

slides.heading: Mine raw materials: value rises to $10 of value
bullets: Lithium and metals are dug out of the ground in Country A - the phone exists only as raw material
The value bar rises to $10, and a route arrow carries the materials on to the next country
slides.notes: Play scene 1 and point to the value bar reaching $10: the first link of the chain is forged at the mine.

slides.heading: Make the components: value rises to $35 of value
bullets: Factories in Country B turn the raw materials into chips, screens and batteries
Making parts adds value: the bar rises to $35, and the components travel on
slides.notes: Play scene 2 and follow the route arrow in: the materials from Country A land as components, and the value rises to $35.

slides.heading: Assemble the phone: value rises to $70 of value
bullets: In Country C the components are assembled into a finished smartphone, so the value bar rises again to $70
Assembly adds more value than any single earlier stage - the parts become one working phone
slides.notes: Play scene 3 and watch the bar: $35 becomes $70 as separate components become a finished phone.

slides.heading: Sell it in Singapore: value rises to $120 of value
bullets: The finished phone is shipped to a shop shelf in Singapore, where transport, branding and retail add the final value
The bar reaches $120 - the selling price carries the value added by all four countries
slides.notes: Play scene 4 and note the careful wording: $120 is the value after every stage, not the value of Singapore work alone.

slides.heading: Worked example: running the whole chain
bullets: Country A $10: raw materials are mined; Country B $35: the materials become components
Country C $70 and Singapore $120: assembly and retail add value at every stage, carried on by the route arrows
slides.notes: Work it slowly: Step 1, Country A $10. Step 2, Country B $35. Step 3, Country C $70. Step 4, Singapore $120. At each step ask: what did this stage add that the stage before could not?

slides.heading: Your turn: run the chain in order
bullets: In pairs: starting from the mine in Country A, state each stage of the chain in order and the value reached at that stage
Then swap and check: did your partner show the product being carried across borders, or made in one place?
slides.notes: Give pairs three minutes. Listen for the full chain in order, then take two pairs answers: Country A $10, Country B $35, Country C $70, Singapore $120, with value rising at each handover.

slides.heading: Exit ticket: prove it before you leave
bullets: Your exit ticket asks you to correct a student who says a global product is made entirely in the country where it is sold
Name the four stages in order and the value added between them to earn full credit
slides.notes: Point to the exit ticket and remind the class: the strongest answers run the chain in order and name what each stage did to the value.
